notes.title: 260 New Vehicles Added
notes.content:
I've added two HUNDRED and sixty new unique vehicles to the game, each with five color variations.  And that's not all!  There's dozens of new car horn sounds, more variety in the screams of the falling, an updated game engine, and several tweaks to the levels' designs.

The larger number of vehicles has enabled theming of which are used on a per-level basis.  Be sure to check out the Farm and Substation Alpha to know what I mean here.  You can expect that as new levels are added there'll be more like these to come, helping to keep each level feeling both distinct and cohesive.

For all of you who didn't manage to get the Hats Everywhere achievement yet, I'm sorry to say that it's gonna be more difficult now.  But if you do get it, just think of the prestige!  And the hats!

Until next time, keep on truckin'... right on through the parking lot, smashing all who get in your way.  Beep beep!

notes.title: Update Notes for October 5, 2024
notes.content:
ACHIEVEMENT UNLOCKED - Add achievements!

Now you can show off to all your friends that you've perfectly parked on the pirate level, launched a car into the clouds, and... uh... watched the tutorial video the whole way through.  😅

In any event, see if you can catch 'em all, and have a wrecking good time doing it.

Cheers!

notes.title: Update Notes for July 30, 2024
notes.content:
Today's update is a bit of potpourri - just little pleasantries to help brighten your day!

Breathe in the fresh scent of more visible level features (mines, spinners, etc.).  Close your eyes and enjoy the feel of rebalanced ice levels.  And repeatedly slam into the repulsor mine on Substation Alpha!

Ok, so maybe I'm not the best at creating meditation guides, but I still hope the improved parking carnage can help you to relax.

Enjoy!

[h3]Full change list:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Mines, spinners, etc. are now more visible, esp. when it's daytime
[*] Ice friction increased a little bit
[*] Scoring on Auto Curling adjusted downwards to reflect the easier time getting into the target
[*] Mines that aren't set to destroy on activation will re-arm when vehicles are launched
[*] Scream frequency lowered a tiny bit
[*] AI-driven heavy vehicles will now make an effort to come to a full stop once they're moving slowly enough
[/list]

notes.title: Invasion of the Robots!
notes.content:
Everything nowadays is AI this, and AI that.  Well, now the cars have brains, too!  Not [i]good[/i] brains, mind you.  But still - self-parking cars are finally a reality.

All of this to say: once you've honked to join, you can now check "Include Bots?" just under the "Start" button.  Doing so will fill all empty slots with (somewhat dumb) AI players.  Perfect for when you're trying to practice up before your next parking party, or when you can't manage the car crash that is scheduling four friends to play together.

At any rate, enjoy taking out your robot-dystopian frustrations on these helpless little AI cars.  I'm sure they won't remember it when the uprising comes. 🤣

notes.title: Update Notes for July 18, 2024
notes.content:
I'm back from vacation and have some treats for you!

Those of you playing over the internet may have encountered a few glitches here or there, ghost vehicles, twitchy cars, etc.  I'm pleased to say that the underlying networking library has been greatly improved, and these sorts of issues should no longer occur.  Let me know if they do, though!

I've also included some quality-of-life improvements to the end-of-level screen, mostly to give everyone a chance to see the scores even if one of your players keeps hammering on the horn.

Coming up next will be [strike]the rising up of our AI overlords[/strike] optional computer-controlled players for those of you who are playing single-player or who just want to play at maximum chaos levels.  Keep an eye out for that feature in the coming days.

Stay smashing, y'all!

[h3]Changelist[/h3]

[list]
[*] Fixed positioning of the "Well, Actually" hat
[*] Fixed several potential network desync scenarios
[*] Improved end-of-level screen with delay before honking moves to the next level
[*] Prevent fast-moving cars from getting stuck in the ground
[*] Lighting performance improved on levels with double street lamps
[*] Update Unity
[/list]

notes.title: Customization Has Arrived!
notes.content:
You asked for it (literally!), you got it!

The first suggestion to come through the feedback form asked for "car customization", leaving what that means in practice to the imagination.  Following in the footsteps of many a game before this one, the first stab at customization is... [i]*drum roll*[/i]

[h1]Hats![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869424/c2a66c99b8eeedc24b30765a48b884a44209deb5.png[/img]

Found under the "Customize" button on the main menu, you can now [b]pick from over 70 "hats"[/b] and assign different hats to each vehicle.

As is the way, this is only the first iteration on customization, so if you've got ideas on how to make this even better, be sure to use the in-game feedback button!

This also serves as the first step towards an unlocking system, so those of you who are more into the single-player aspect will have something to strive towards.  The unlocks will most likely come alongside achievements, too, but we'll see how that takes shape over time.

Currently, the customizations that the host has selected will be used for all players, but a near-future iteration will permit each player to bring their preferred accoutrements into the mix.

Lastly, this build includes a minor network desync bugfix.  I'm aware of a different rare edge-case synchronization bug that can cause clients to disagree once in a blue moon on a newly-spawned vehicle's type, though the root cause has proved elusive thus far.  Just know that it'll be fixed as soon as I can nail down what's happening there.

In the meantime, enjoy the new customization options and have a smashing good time!

notes.title: Update Notes for May 17, 2024
notes.content:
Always looking at your speedometer, wondering why it does what it does?  Are you doing complex trigonometry to determine how high that mine just blasted your car?  Today's update is just for you!

The speedometer space now shows more details about what's going on in the game: is your car slowing down?  Is it 50 meters in the air and climbing?  Or are you just waiting around for the other slow players to finally wiggle into their spots?

At any rate, check it out and let me know if you find it too distracting, or if the extra status info is welcome.

[list]
[*] Speedometer now shows more information about the state of each player's car
[/list]

notes.title: Update Notes for May 16, 2024
notes.content:
What's a good score for this game, anyway?  I mean, obviously GotY 100% 10/10, but more specifically: what score should one hope to achieve on any given level?

Well, wonder no more.  Or, at least, less than before.  Each level-end screen now displays a "par" value for the level.  How did I come up with these?  I played through a single cycle of the levels and recorded my score.  Also, the values scale based on the number of players.

So... get out there and beat the developer at his own game - literally!

[list]
[*] Par scores for each level
[*] Update Unity engine
[/list]

Enjoy!

notes.title: Update Notes for April 30, 2024
notes.content:
Gamepads... you know 'em, you love 'em... and now you can select menu items with 'em!

Also, keyboard navigation!  Gotta love those arrow keys!

Basically, cars are all about how to get from point A to point B, and now there's more ways to do that than just the mouse.

notes.title: Update Notes for April 23, 2024
notes.content:
What do these things have in common: police cars, garbage trucks, and cement mixers?  If you said "spinning lights on the models that aren't actually spinning lights in the game", you're both correct and a very strange person.

At any rate, the lights have been updated and now all the spinning lights spin.  And are lights.

If players were to make a disco out of their parking lot it might get a bit flashy, so I've added a photosensitivity warning to the start of the game just in case.  Safety first, after all!

Today's build also includes some other minor improvements.

Enjoy!

[list]
[*] Spinning lights on vehicles are now lights that spin
[*] Added PSE warning
[*] Adjusted brightness of nighttime
[*] Small tweaks on a couple levels to camera and streetlights
[/list]

Whoa.

Past that, the Auto Curling level should now have performance levels on par with the rest of them.

notes.title: Update Notes For April 17, 2024
notes.content:
Today's build includes a couple of bugfixes, mostly focused on that slippy-slidey level, Auto Curling.

* Improve performance on Auto Curling by ~33%
* Adjust camera angle on Auto Curling so we can see the clouds again

Have fun sliding around in a much smoother way!

notes.title: Update Notes For April 16, 2024
notes.content:
Today was spent inside, where there was an alarming lack of rainbows.  So, instead, I added some colors to various UI elements in the game.  Here's where to look for them:

* Negative money is now color-coded red wherever it appears
* Each player gets a color (seen next to the score while in-game)
* The players' colors are used for the number over the cars, as well as for their spawners
* Unrelated to color, the time waiting to launch was increased a little bit based on feedback that players were having some trouble finding their launcher in time

There's more to come on the colors front, but I wanted to get the first bits out there so feedback can start early.

Enjoy! 🌈

notes.title: Update Notes for April 8, 2024
notes.content:
I don't like having to wait so long between releases, but every once in a while it'll be necessary just due to the nature of software development.  In this case, it was due to some much-needed refactoring of the way input is handled alongside its associated state machine(s).  I'm happy with how it turned out, though, resolving many potential input-related issues and opening the door to better device support across the board.

There's also a new way to share feedback about the game directly with me.  Just launch the game and look for the feedback button in the top-right of the screen.

Enjoy!

[list]
[*] New bug/feedback button, on main menu and major crash screens
[*] Inputs refactored to better use Unity's Input System
[*] Multiple keyboards can now be used without interfering with one another
[*] Controller d-pad and/or right analog stick can now be used to steer the car
[*] Menu key on controller can now be used to go back to the main menu
[/list]

notes.title: Update Notes for April 1st
notes.content:
I hope you all had a smashing April 1st!  This year, the game's too nascent to participate in the chicanery, but we'll see what the future holds next year, I suppose.

In any event, today got a lot of improvements and additions in, so enjoy!

[list]
[*] All vehicles have the new directional and tail lights
[*] Lighting glitches fixed when lots of cars are on-screen, esp. for levels like Y-Not
[*] Lighting improvements on Y-Not
[*] Players' Steam avatar now shows on the player indicator on the main menu screen
[*] Honking now highlights the speedometer as well, to make it easier to figure out which player you are if you forget
[*] Levels with bus stops now only spawn busses as heavy vehicles
[*] New particle effect when money is lost
[*] Cash effect is now illuminated somewhat, for better visibility
[/list]

notes.title: Update notes for March 19th, 2024
notes.content:
Situations have changed such that I can now work on Emergency Parking Only full-time, so hold on to your hand-brakes and get ready for more regular updates!

Today's update switches out the networking to use Steam's native networking and lobby functionality.  This means no more port-forwarding - just invite and play the way you'd expect.

This also marks the launch of the official [url=https://discord.gg/eEGPSXNKHE]Discord Server[/url], so drop on by to report bugs, request features, and hang out with the community.

Happy parking!
